clue.text: Lock given order to be quiet!

definitions.meaning: to lock a house or a prisoner away is to secure it fast
the curt command telling someone to stop talking

explanation.surface: A rugby lock forward is told by the referee to hold his tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: In this rugby-themed puzzle 'Lock' looks like the forward position, but it is the verb meaning secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idiomatic: to lock something away, and the blunt command for silence.

clue.text: Do something in scrum, resulting in punch

definitions.meaning: the ... job in a scrum is to heel the ball back with the foot
a boxer's curved blow thrown from the side

explanation.surface: A forward does something in the scrum that ends in a fist being thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooking the ball is the hooker's scrum task, and a hook is a type of boxing blow.

clue.text: Value of three goals in this game

definitions.meaning: in rugby union a converted try (a goal) is worth seven points, so three are worth this many
the card game also called pontoon or blackjack

explanation.surface: A remark on how many points three goals are worth in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: A converted try is 5 + 2 = 7 points; three make the number. The card game, also known as pontoon, carries the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times seven gives the number, which is also the name of the card game pontoon.

clue.text: Literary work of American author on success in rugby

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of tales and verse
a try, grounding the ball over the line, is rugby's chief scoring success

explanation.surface: A literary piece by an American writer about scoring in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is literary work, and the general noun covers it as a body of writing.

clue.text: Burden on shoulders of scrum-half, say, and forwards

parts.note: the scrum-half is one of the backs, the team's non-forward players
the forwards collectively form the pack

explanation.surface: Rugby players carry a load on their shoulders, as backs and forwards do in a team.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is the load carried on the shoulders and back.

clue.text: Where 8 goes (as roughly depicted) when one's temporarily not working?

definitions.meaning: a successful kick at goal passes between the uprights
between jobs, that is between posts or positions of employment

explanation.surface: The conversion kick sails through the uprights, just as an unemployed person drifts between jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is CONVERSION, which must go through the uprights. 'As roughly depicted' refers to the grid, where this entry runs down beside it; posts here are also jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal kick must go through the uprights, and being between jobs is to be out of work.

clue.text: Fruits of careful intensive training initially with stratagems

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the three words before it

parts.note: ruses are tricks or stratagems

explanation.surface: Results come from careful, intensive training and clever tactics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruits' reads as results of training, but it is the literal definition: oranges and lemons.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges, lemons and limes are the fruit family named here, plural to match.

clue.text: Strength shown by guy in red under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue this piece sits under the pressure letter, so it follows it

parts.note: someone in the red is in debt, a person who owes

explanation.surface: A man in a red shirt shows his strength when put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In red' looks like a team colour, but it means in debt, so the guy is one who owes.
explanation.definitionFit: Power and strength are close synonyms for force or might.

clue.text: Change that's passed over the bar, as seen here

definitions.meaning: an alteration from one form to another

definitions.text: that's passed over the bar, as seen here
definitions.meaning: the kick after a try that must clear the crossbar; 'as seen here' points to 23, which turns 25 into 22

explanation.surface: A rugby fan remarks that the ball sails over the crossbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformation is a change, and in rugby the post-try kick has the same name.

clue.text: Passage of play after instant opening lets me in

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the instant

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

indicators.note: lets ... in means the opening admits the following word inside it
completes 'lets ... in', placing the word me inside the opening

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A phase of rugby where play, after a quick gap, lets a player through.
explanation.definitionFit: A section of a symphony or other musical work is a movement, a passage of the piece played.

clue.text: Pulling in direction of player on side

parts.note: to means towards, in the direction of
a wing plays on the side of the pitch

explanation.surface: A winger drags play towards the side of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Towing is drawing a vehicle along behind, which is pulling it.

clue.text: About to enter the area of town centre, perhaps

indicators.note: to enter means this piece goes inside the following words

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning
a quarter is a district of a town

explanation.surface: Something approaches the middle of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Town centre' looks like a single phrase, but 'town' belongs to the wordplay and 'centre' is a rugby position, one of the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre is one of the backs known by this position name, so 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: Peter with men in resort, having no match

indicators.note: to re-sort letters is to rearrange them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Peter is staying with some men at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place, but read as re-sort it is the anagram signal for PETER MEN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outstanding above all others means having no match.

clue.text: Players in front row, say, of small musical group

definitions.meaning: a scrum's front row is three players: two props and a hooker

explanation.surface: The front-row forwards of a scrum form a little band.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum's front row is three players, and three musicians make up this group.

clue.text: Extremely poor English side, awfully restricted in score

indicators.note: restricted in means held inside the following word

parts.note: to net is to score a goal

indicators.note: awfully signals the letters are jumbled badly

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An English team plays terribly, kept to a tiny score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' looks like a noun for points, but it is the verb meaning to put the ball in the goal. 'Awfully' makes EDIES, placed after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of needy means poorest of all, extremely poor.

clue.text: Where scrum-half's expertise lies, by the way

definitions.meaning: the scrum-half's skill is in moving the ball on to the backs

explanation.surface: A remark that a scrum-half's real skill is in distribution.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum-half excels at distributing the ball, and the phrase also means incidentally.

clue.text: Fantastic crowd puller? Not half!

indicators.note: fantastic shapes the letters into a fanciful new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the word is kept, its first three letters

explanation.surface: An excited claim that a tournament draws huge crowds, with 'Not half!' meaning absolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' drops the second half of PULLER, leaving PUL, which 'Fantastic' mixes with CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby's world tournament is a huge draw for spectators, a crowd puller indeed.

clue.text: One insect after another buzzing round head of hooker, huge fellow

indicators.note: the first insect is placed after the other
buzzing round means this insect surrounds the next piece

parts.note: a bee is a second kind of insect

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word after it

parts.note: a moth is an insect

explanation.surface: Insects buzz round a rugby hooker, a giant of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a monstrous beast in the Bible, so by extension anything or anyone enormous.

clue.text: Player essential in pack for power

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A forward is vital to the pack for its strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is one of the forwards who anchor the scrum, an essential part of the pack.

clue.text: Fine player that contributes significantly to result

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an actor plays parts

explanation.surface: A good player makes a big difference to the score.
explanation.definitionFit: A factor is an element or cause that helps bring about an outcome.

clue.text: Dramatic and inspiring performances, specially with arm broken

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed apart and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Outstanding games played by a team member with a broken arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic and inspiring performances' sounds like great matches; it means the medieval Bible dramas about saints' wonders.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval dramas showing saints' wondrous deeds were plays meant to inspire faith.

clue.text: Arguing with referee extremely unwise, ultimately — don't show dissent

indicators.note: extremely picks the first and last letters of each word
ultimately picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice that arguing with the referee is foolish: hold your tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur rather than object is not to show dissent.

clue.text: Hurt repeatedly as part of approaches coaches used

indicators.note: the answer sits inside each of the two words in turn

explanation.surface: Injuries keep coming from the training methods coaches use.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt with a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: 25 to 22 as result of this conversion

definitions.text: 25 to 22 as result of this conversion

parts.words: 25 to 22 as result of this conversion
parts.note: rugby's old 25-yard line became the 22-metre line when units changed from imperial

explanation.surface: A puzzling sum: 25 becoming 22 through a change.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers look like scores, but the change is from yards to metres, which renamed rugby's 25 as the 22.
explanation.definitionFit: Going from yards to metres is the change to the decimal system of measurement.

clue.text: Position man in back row at start of game for scrum, say

parts.note: to set is to position or place

parts.words: man in back row at start of game
parts.note: in chess the pieces (as opposed to pawns) begin the game on the back row

explanation.surface: A coach positions a back-row forward at the start of the match to scrum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back row' looks like rugby's back-row forwards, but it is the chessboard rank where pieces stand at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is a planned restart of play, an example of a rehearsed move, hence 'say'.

clue.text: After a time, leads on tries

indicators.note: after places the enticing piece after the article and time letter

parts.note: to lead someone on is to tempt them

explanation.surface: After a while, a team leading goes on to score tries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' reads as rugby scores, but it is the plural noun meaning efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tries in the sense of efforts are attempts.

clue.text: In which oval object is passed around in play

definitions.text: In which oval object is passed around in play

indicators.note: in places the turned object inside the play's title

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that introduced the word robot

indicators.note: passed around means the object is turned back to front

parts.note: an egg is oval

explanation.surface: A description of the game in which an oval ball is passed around.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is a 1920 Czech play by Karel Capek; the clue as a whole describes the game itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial British name for rugby union, played with an oval ball that is passed.
